newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LYLE BRAVES JINX, WINS MASTERS' PAR 3 CONTEST.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LYLE BRAVES JINX, WINS MASTERS' PAR 3 CONTEST.

text.p: Briton Sandy Lyle won the annual Par 3 Contest at Augusta National on Wednesday and immediately became the biggest longshot at the 61st Masters starting on Thursday.
Lyle, the 1988 Masters champion, became the first European player ever to win the crystal trophy, but gained the burden of the Par 3 jinx as well.
None of the previous 37 winners of the contest, held on the eve of the Masters on the nine-hole course adjacent to the famed Augusta National layout, has ever gone on to win the major championship.
Last year's winner, Jay Haas, finished tied for 36th.

Lyle and Mark McNulty of Zimbabwe were tied after nine holes at five-under-par 22. They both parred the first extra hole but McNulty found the water with his tee shot on the second playoff hole after Lyle had put his ball within two feet.
This year's Par 3 Contest, always a lighthearted affair and a treat for practice day spectators, featured a couple of celebrity caddies.
David Robinson, the injured star centre for the NBA's San Antonio Spurs, carried friend Corey Pavin's bag, and rock musician Glenn Frey, formerly of the Eagles, toted for Brad Faxon.
